intro: Legionella bacteria can grow in building water systems and cause Legionnaires' disease, a serious lung infection you help prevent.
points: People catch Legionnaires' disease by breathing in contaminated water droplets, often from showers; it cannot pass between people.
Report anyone with flu-like symptoms, cough or breathlessness promptly to a senior colleague or nurse so medical help is arranged.
Legionella multiplies fastest in warm, stagnant water between 20 and 45 degrees; keep hot water hot and cold water cold.
Flush little-used taps and showers to keep water moving, and descale showerheads regularly; always record the tasks you complete.
Report lukewarm water, discoloured water, odd smells or heavily scaled showerheads to the responsible person straight away.
The duty holder and responsible person manage the risk assessment; your part is assigned tasks, records and reporting concerns.
